title: Tom's published compositions
summary: Tom's songs such as June, Rose of Spain and Love Dreams; uncertainty about Bungalow of Dreams.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: One question here about some of Tom's pieces. Do you remember some of his titles, the pieces that he wrote?

Yes, he had some numbers that he published. And I don't know, he didn't have them in the hands of the right people. They weren't plugged much. The only one that plugged it was him himself. I didn't, I myself, I didn't think much of them. I didn't think that they had any good commercial value to them. So, but let him have his fun, you know. There's a lot of people that write numbers, you know what I mean? That's mean anything. But he did have some numbers, wrote some numbers and had them published.
Do you remember the number June?

Yeah. And he had something to do with, what's the Spanish number? Rose of Spain. Rose of Spain. We have a piano roll of that, Love Dreams. He had some, did he have, did he put that on Rolls, Love Dreams? Yeah.
And the Halfway House recorded Love Dreams too, I believe.
Do you remember a piece, Our Bungalow of Dreams?
Bungalow of Dreams, yes I remember that.
Is that his, do you think? It was by a brown, but it has an E on the end of it.

Yeah, well, it seemed like I heard Tom speak of that, but now whether that's his or not I couldn't say. I've never seen the music to it or anything, but I've heard Tom speak of it. That's right. There's another brown with E on it, that means he's Irish. And we're English, so the B-R-O-W-N's. Yeah. And if he puts E on it, it's Irish. But I heard Tom speak about that, now whether he wrote it, I don't think he did.
